title: sre-weekly-update-2026-08-22
summary: Weekly SRE update covering incidents, SLO status, recent on-call handoffs, and action items for the coming week.
content:
SRE Weekly Update — 2026-08-22

Owner: Aisha Patel (eng-sre)
Collaborators: Miguel Torres, Jordan Kim, Priya Shah
Status: Final

1) Highlights / TL;DR
- One Sev2 incident (INC-2026-1123) impacting hosted-api write path on 2026-08-20 for ~47 minutes; degraded throughput and higher tail latency. Root cause: autoscaler misconfiguration + race condition in cache priming.
- All customer-facing SLOs on track this week except API 99th latency for small text gen (missed by 0.6 percentage points during the incident window).
- On-call rotation completed with a clean handoff; updated runbooks for cache priming and autoscaler thresholds.

2) Incident(s) summary
INC-2026-1123 — 2026-08-20 14:12 UTC -> 15:00 UTC (47 minutes)
- Impact: Hosted API customers saw increased 95/99 p99 latency and several throttled requests for the text-generate write path in us-west-2. No data exposure. Several larger enterprise customers reported timeouts and elevated error rates.
- Detection: Pager triggered by elevated 99p latency alert + customer tickets.
- What happened: During a routine autoscaler config rollout, a new threshold meant small-burst traffic did not trigger fast-enough scaling. At the same time, cache-priming job hit a race where KV cache entries were evicted before warm-up completed, causing many cold-starts. Combined effect created head-of-line latency.
- Mitigation timeline:
  - 14:15 UTC: On-call (Miguel) acknowledged incident and switched scale policy to conservative fallback.
  - 14:22 UTC: Temporarily increased min replicas for text-gen autopool in us-west-2.
  - 14:35 UTC: Restarted cache-priming job with sequential warmup to avoid evictions.
  - 14:45 UTC: Error rate and 99p latency trending back to normal.
  - 15:00 UTC: Incident declared resolved.
- Root cause: autoscaler config change + cache-priming race. Root-cause confirmed in postmortem.
- Action items (see below) and postmortem drafted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-2026-1123-postmortem

3) SLOs / Metrics
- Hosted API - availability (5m window): 99.996% (target 99.95%) — PASS
- Hosted API - text-gen p99 latency (30d trailing): 1.12s (target <=1.0s) — WARNING (regression driven by the incident spike; ongoing monitoring)
- Embeddings API - error rate: 0.02% (target <=0.1%) — PASS
- Internal infra (control plane) - deploy success rate: 99.8% (target 99.9%) — INVESTIGATING (deploy flakiness noticed for blue/green swaps; ticketed SRE-347)
Notes: The p99 latency miss is concentrated in the us-west-2 region and during burst windows. We are tracking with increased sampling and rolling window alerting for regional p99s.

4) On-call handoffs and rotations
- Rotation: 2026-08-16 -> 2026-08-22 completed. Outgoing on-call: Miguel Torres. Incoming on-call: Jordan Kim.
- Handoff notes (brief):
  - Miguel: left a reminder in runbook about autoscaler flag rollback steps and the temporary console overrides used during INC-2026-1123.
  - Jordan: to monitor the new smoke test rollout scheduled 2026-08-23 for small-burst traffic behavior.
- Pager noise: We saw an uptick in noisy alerts from the autoscaler health check — cleaning thresholds to reduce noise this week.

5) Runbook and tooling updates
- Updated runbook: cache-priming -> added sequential warm-up example and safe restart checklist (Confluence link in linked_artifacts).
- Added a fallback autoscaler policy that keeps a conservative min_replicas during config rollouts; documented the CLI rollback flow in runbook.
- Internal tool: increased sampling in the latency profiler on text-gen routes to 5x for the next 72 hours.

6) Action items and owners
- SRE-348 (Owner: Priya Shah): Add test coverage for autoscaler threshold changes in staging; due 2026-09-03.
- SRE-349 (Owner: Miguel Torres): Implement a canary for cache-priming job restarts that validates KV retention; due 2026-08-29.
- SRE-350 (Owner: Jordan Kim): Tighten regional p99 alerting and add 15m heatmap to dashboard; due 2026-08-27.
- SRE-351 (Owner: Aisha Patel): Run a war-room drill on prefer-local routing and validate fallback model variants; scheduled 2026-09-07.

7) Upcoming work / risks
- Deploying the new autoscaler rollout strategy across all regions (risk window: 2026-08-25 -> 2026-08-28). Will schedule staggered rollouts and extra on-call coverage.
- Planned maintenance: control-plane DB index rebuild on 2026-08-26 (low traffic window). Coordinating with infra and product teams.
- Risk: continued small-burst traffic patterns from a new customer workload — could produce similar head-of-line latencies if not covered by the warmup canary. Prioritizing canary development.

8) Blockers / asks from other teams
- Product-hosted-api: Need a short-lived quota increase for two enterprise customers while we validate the conservative autoscaler policy. (Assigned to Aisha to coordinate)
- Observability: Requesting an additional 7-day retention for trace sampling during the autoscaler rollout (ticketed OBS-122).

9) Misc / notes to self
- Remember to add postmortem action items to the SRE board and tag owners.
- Consider adding a synthetic small-burst test to CI to catch regressions earlier.

If you have questions or want a deep-dive on any section, ping the SRE Slack channel (#sre-ops) or comment on the Confluence postmortem.

-- Aisha
